verdict.rationale: Angular's docs suggest a low barrier to entry ('Get started in 5 minutes', in-browser tutorial), but hands-on community reports concretely contradict the 'standard HTML/CSS/JS' framing: Angular's template syntax (*ngFor, [title]) is explicitly called invalid HTML/XML that breaks standard tooling, templates-as-strings block normal editor support, and the framework requires learning TypeScript, decorators, dependency injection, and has historically shifted between JS/Dart/AtScript/TypeScript, adding real new concepts beyond vanilla web syntax. Missing for 10: first-party acknowledgment of these syntax/tooling gaps, evidence of using truly standard HTML/CSS without extension, and independent confirmation the learning curve is minimal.
